findings.title: Apply the saved timeout to the shutdown drain
findings.problem: POSTing shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 now persists successfully, but shutdown still calls asyncio.timeout(_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT) at triggarr/search/scheduler.py:634. That constant reads only the environment and otherwise defaults to 60 seconds (lines 58–81). With no environment override, the requested 120.5-second drain therefore still forces resource closure after 60 seconds.

members.title: Saving settings resets shutdown_drain_timeout to 60.0 because the form has no input for it
members.problem: save_settings reads form.get("shutdown_drain_timeout"), but no template contains a field with that name: grep for 'drain' under triggarr/templates/ returns nothing. form.get therefore returns None, and safe_float (validation.py:224-225) returns the hardcoded default 60.0. As a result, every POST /settings, including one that only changes an unrelated field, writes 60.0 to config.toml and overwrites whatever the operator set (for example 300.0 in TOML). The settings_page context at line 446 also passes the value to a template that never renders it. Another field the form does not carry, tracking_delay_seconds at line 548, avoids this by falling back to current_settings.general.*. tests/test_web.py:694 expects the input on the settings page and will fail.
members.why_it_matters: A configured drain timeout is silently lost on any settings save, so in-flight searches get cut off at shutdown sooner than the operator intended.
members.fix_hint: add the numeric input to settings.html, and/or use current_settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout as the safe_float default so a missing field keeps the saved value

members.title: Every settings save resets shutdown_drain_timeout to 60.0 because the form does not have this input yet
members.problem: The POST handler now reads form.get("shutdown_drain_timeout"). triggarr/templates/settings.html has no input with that name: a grep finds only max_consecutive_failures at settings.html:74. The submitted form never carries the field, so safe_float(None, 60.0, ...) returns 60.0. Every settings save then writes 60.0 back to the TOML and overwrites whatever value the operator had set, for example 120. In this working tree the GET test at tests/test_web.py:694, which asserts the input is rendered, also fails. Plan 75-02 Task 2 (adding the template input) is still pending, so this diff is half of a two-part change.
members.why_it_matters: If this is committed or pushed alone, every settings save silently clobbers a config value and the test suite fails. The runtime effect is limited for now because the scheduler still reads only the env var.
members.fix_hint: Land the settings.html input (75-02 Task 2) in the same commit. Or fall back to current_settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout when the field is missing, which is the pattern tracking_delay_seconds uses.

members.title: Supported config values above 3600 are silently clamped down on any settings save
members.problem: GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout (models/config.py:139) is Field(ge=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False) with no upper bound, so a TOML value such as 7200.0 is valid. The form handler clamps to 3600.0. Once the template input exists, it is pre-filled with 7200, so submitting the settings form for an unrelated change rewrites the value to 3600. While the input is missing, the value becomes 60.0 instead (see bugs-001). The comment at config.py:138 says the UI ceiling is intentional, but the stored value still changes without the user acting on that field.
members.why_it_matters: An operator's long drain timeout is quietly cut to 3600 seconds after an unrelated settings edit.
members.fix_hint: either add le=3600.0 to the model so the contract matches the UI, or set the form clamp max to at least the model's range

members.title: Persisted drain timeout is never used; scheduler still reads the import-time env constant
members.problem: The scheduler uses the module-level _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT (scheduler.py:81, used at 611-656). That constant is computed once at import from TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT and never reads settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout. The value saved here has no effect at runtime, even though the design spec says it must be read from settings at scheduler setup or shutdown time. pending: confirm the scheduler wiring is not planned for a later wave of phase 75 that has not landed yet.
members.why_it_matters: Users change a setting in the UI and nothing changes at runtime.
members.fix_hint: read settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout at shutdown time, with the env var as an override on top

members.title: Form cap of 3600 silently lowers valid config values above 3600 on any settings save
members.problem: GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout (models/config.py:139) only sets ge=1.0 and allow_inf_nan=False, with no upper bound, so a TOML value of 7200.0 is valid. routes.py:550 caps it with max=3600.0. An operator with 7200 in config.toml who saves the settings page for any unrelated reason has the drain timeout silently cut to 3600. Once the planned template input exists with max="3600" (75-02-PLAN.md:157), the browser's constraint validation will block form submission whenever the rendered value is above 3600 or does not fit step="0.5" (for example 120.25), and the whole settings page becomes unsaveable.
members.why_it_matters: The bound applies only when the form is saved, not when config loads, so values the config contract accepts change silently, and a future template could lock the settings form.
members.fix_hint: Make the model and the form agree on bounds: add le=3600.0 to the Field, or drop the form ceiling. Use step="any" in the template input.

findings.title: Add the timeout input to the settings template
findings.problem: The added context variable is never consumed by triggarr/templates/settings.html: there is no shutdown_drain_timeout input. Browser users cannot view or submit this setting, and subsequent browser saves replace a value submitted directly to the endpoint with the 60-second fallback. The existing test_settings_page_renders_new_config_fields assertion also requires this missing input.
